Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:2.english: And make a hole in it - Into its interior, he should hollow out a cavity within it.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:3.hebrew: וליתבה בי מיללי דנורא - מניחו ע"ג גחלים לוחשות, שיתבשל האתרוג בדבש:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:3.english: And place it among burning coals - He places it upon glowing coals, so that the citron cooks in the honey.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:4.hebrew: בני מ' יום - שעברו עליהם מ' יום. ל"א, של תינוק בן מ' יום:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:4.english: Forty days old - That forty days have passed over it. Another interpretation: [Urine] of a forty-day-old infant.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:6.hebrew: ברזינא לזיבורא - כוס קטן מאד ושמו ברזינא, מאותן מי רגלים שותין למי שנשכתו צרעה ומתרפא:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:6.english: Barzina for a hornet - A very small cup, whose name is barzina, of that urine — they drink [it] for one whom a hornet has stung, and he is healed.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:7.english: A quarter, for a scorpion - A quarter of a log for one whom a scorpion has stung.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:8.english: Half a riv'a for exposed [water] - Half a log.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:9.hebrew: אניגרון ואבנגר ותירייקי - מים שנשלק בהם בנגרי, מין עשב ששמו בנגרי. וסתם אניגרון — מי שלק תרדין, כדאמרינן (ברכות דף לה:): אניגרון — מיא דסילקא. ותירייקי — צרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:10:9.english: Anigron, avangar, and tiryaka - [Avangar is] water in which bangari was boiled, a type of herb whose name is bangari. And ordinary anigron [is] the water of boiled beets, as we say (Berakhot 35b): "Anigron is the water of beets." And tiryaka [is] balsam.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:11:2.hebrew: אידמי ליה כפרשא - תופסו ומייסרו, שהפחד והמרוצה והכשות מתישין כחו ומחמם, ומת הנחש בתוכו:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:11:2.english: He appeared to him as a horseman - seizing him and afflicting him, for the fear, the running, and the hops weaken its strength and heat [it] up, and the snake dies inside him.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:11:3.hebrew: גובי - חתיכות חתיכות, יצא הנחש ממנו. גובי — טרונצו"ץ בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:11:3.english: Gubei [pieces] - Pieces, pieces — the snake came out of him. Gubei [is] tronçons in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:11:5.english: A fetus of a white donkey - A fetus that is found in the womb of a white female donkey.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:11:6.english: That is not found [to be] tereifah - [Referring to] the mother.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:1:1.english: Say that they disagree with regard to impurity and purity - And [they disagree] because of a verse.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:1:2.hebrew: לענין שבת - דטעמא משום רפואה הוא, מי שמעת להו:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:1:2.english: With regard to Shabbat - where the reason is on account of healing, did you hear them [disagree]?

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:1:3.hebrew: הא דאישתהי - בגוייהו אסור, דמוכחא מלתא דלרפואה קא מכוין:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:1:3.english: This [refers to a case] where one remained - in them [the waters], it is prohibited, for it is evident that he intends [it] for healing.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:1:4.hebrew: הא דלא אישתהי - אלא רחץ ויצא, מותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:1:4.english: That [case] where he did not linger - rather, he bathed and exited, [it is] permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:2:1.english: The last [baraita] - Which teaches "one may bathe" [refers to a case] where one did not remain.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:2:3.hebrew: שלא נשתהי - בתוך המים, דנראה כמיקר בעלמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:2:3.english: Where one did not remain - in the water, for he appears merely as one cooling himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:3:1.english: In the good [waters] - For [people] bathe in them on a weekday for bathing that is not for healing.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:3:2.hebrew: ברעים - אין רוחצין, דמוכחא מלתא דלרפואה, ותרוייהו בדאישתהי:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:3:2.english: In the bad [waters] - One may not bathe, because it is evident that [it is] for healing, and both [statements] are [referring to a case] where one lingered [in the water].

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:3:3.hebrew: מי המשרה אמי המשרה לא קשיא - הך דקתני רוחצין במי המשרה, אהנך תרתי דלעיל דקתני אבל לא במי המשרה — הא דאישתהי, הא דלא אשתהי:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:3:3.english: Water of soaking [versus] water of soaking is not difficult - This [baraita] that teaches, "One may bathe in water of soaking," [as opposed] to those two [baraitot] above that teach, "but not in water of soaking" — this [is where] he lingered, [and] that [is where] he did not linger.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:4:1.hebrew: איזביון - מפרש בגמרא, שאינו מאכל בריאים, ומוכחא מלתא דלרפואה אכיל ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:4:1.english: Eizoveyon - [It] is explained in the Gemara; because it is not food for healthy people, it is evident that one eats it for healing.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:4:2.english: However, one may eat yo'ezer - because many [people] eat it when they are healthy.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:4:3.english: [Except] for water from palm trees - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:4:4.hebrew: וכוס עיקרין - משקה שכותשין לתוכו עיקרי ירקות ובשמים, ובגמרא מפרש ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:4:4.english: And a kos ikarin [cup of roots] - A beverage into which one crushes roots of herbs and spices, and in the Gemara [it] explains it.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:4:5.hebrew: מפני שהן לירוקה - לחולי של ירקון, ואינו מאכל בריאים:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:4:5.english: Because they are for yeroka - For the illness of jaundice, and it is not a food of healthy people.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:4:6.english: For his thirst - If he is not ill.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:1.hebrew: אמר רב יוסף אזוב - דאורייתא שהוכשר להזאה, הוא שקורין אברתא בר המג:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:1.english: Rav Yosef said: Hyssop - [The hyssop] of the Torah, which is fit for sprinkling, is what they call abarta bar hamag.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:2.hebrew: איזביון - דמתניתין, הוא שקורין אברתא בר הינג. ויש מרבותי מפרשים: בר המג — שגדל במקום גמי; בר הינג — שגדל בין ההגים, רונצ"ץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:2.english: Eizoveyon - [That] of our Mishnah is what they call abarta bar hing. And some of my teachers explain: bar hamag — [meaning] that it grows in a place of reeds; bar hing — [meaning] that it grows among thorns, ronces [in Old French, brambles].

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:3.hebrew: עולא אמר - אזוב דאורייתא הוא מרוא חיורא, בלע"ז שלוי"א:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:3.english: Ulla said - [The] hyssop of the Torah is marva chivara, in Old French: salvia [sage].

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:4.english: Shumeshuk - It is the hyssop of the Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:5.hebrew: ג' קלחים - דאגודה כתיב, ואין אגודה פחות מג':
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:5.english: Three branches - For "bundle" is written [in Scripture], and a bundle is not less than three.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:6.hebrew: ובהן ג' גבעולין - בכל קלח ג' גבעולין, קנים דקים כעין של קנבוס:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:6.english: And on them three stems - In each branch [there are] three stems, [which are] thin stalks like [those] of hemp.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:5:8.english: That forty days have passed over it - Since it was ground.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:6:2.english: For arketa - Worms that are in the liver.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:6:3.english: From what does [it] come - The illness.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:6:5.english: On an empty stomach - Before eating.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:6:6.english: And from fenugreek shoots - Shoots of fenugreek, like vine shoots.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:6:8.english: And drinking water after them - One who eats one of these before eating and drinks water after it.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:1.hebrew: ואי לא - אי לית ליה פותנק, א"נ אכליה ולא איתסי:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:1.english: And if not - If he does not have potnak, or else [if] he ate it and was not healed.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:10.hebrew: מפני אפשיחה - מקום שנפשח הדקל, אישברנקי"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:10.english: He defecates on the afshicha - A place where the palm tree was split [or had a branch torn off]; [in Old French,] esbranchier.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:3.english: He should suck a bone - He should suck a good limb from that meat and suck its fat with his mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:4.english: Scrapings of a thornbush - Bark scraped from the thornbush.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:5.english: From top to bottom - That it should be scraped from top to bottom.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:6.english: Lest [they] come out - [This refers to] the worms.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:7.english: Through his mouth - By way of his mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:8.hebrew: בי שבבי - בין השמשות, בחשכותא דשמשי. ל"א: בי שבבי — בבית אחד משכניו, שלא יריח הוא הריח שהוא קשה לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:8.english: Bei shivavei - Twilight, at the darkening of the sun. Another explanation: Bei shivavei [means] in the house of one of his neighbors, so that he will not smell the odor, which is harmful to him.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:9.hebrew: נסכרינן לנקבים דיליה - יסתום נחיריו שלא יריח. ל"א: יסתום נחיריו ונקבי אזניו, שלא יצא כח המשקה מגופו:
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:7:9.english: [Let him] close his orifices - He should stop up his nostrils so that he does not smell [it]. Another version: He should stop up his nostrils and the openings of his ears, so that the potency of the potion does not leave his body.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:8:1.english: A solitary staff - A tree that grows alone without a branch.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:8:2.english: For exposed [water] - [For] one who drank exposed water.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:8:5.hebrew: עד דקיימי אאנפקא - שיעמדו על מדה מחזקת אנפק, והיא רביעית הלוג, כדאמרינן בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב נח:):
Rashi on Shabbat 109b:8:5.english: Until they stand at an anpak - That they should stand at a measure holding an anpak, which is a quarter of a log, as we say in [the chapter] Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 58b).

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:9:1.english: And she heated the oven - She heated an oven.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:9:2.english: And she swept it - of coals, so that it would cool down a little.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:9:3.english: And she placed a brick inside it - So that he would sit on it and not be burned.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:9:4.english: And there emerged from him - He vomited the venom that he had swallowed.

Rashi on Shabbat 109b:9:5.english: Hutza - A leaf of a lulav.
